details:
Hi There,

I'd like to have standard unity collider events exposed to further allow avatar creativity. I'm currently being very limited as to what I can do with what's available. I've made myself a shield that I'd like to trigger an animation every time someone or something collides with it.

As an example, when a player fires a weapon, it will impact the shield and trigger an animation, such as a ripple effect using the contact point as a point of reference.

Since custom scripts are forbidden on avatars, it's basically near impossible to achieve this. Contact receiver/sender only supports touch-related actions (IE: hands, feet, fingers, etc)or if an object has the contact with the same custom name. However, this will not work as far as I know when it comes to particle collision detection and anything else.

One simple thing that could be done, is to create a component for the SDK that simply fires a trigger parameter in the animator controller if a collider detects something via one of it's events. Then, a player in unity can access this parameter as a read-only type and use it to perform various interactions. The contact point could also be exposed via readonly parameters.

I hope this can be implemented to allow for more creativity on avatars.
title: Expose Collider Events for avatar creativity
